_comment: Pre-written answers for the build-from-design Tier-3 scenario (#14/#15). Unlike a spec-driven benchmark, the requirements come from the DESIGN dropped in documentation/design/ (mockup.html, tokens.css, design-notes.md) — the workflow reads it at Intake and reads it back for confirmation. These answers only fill the gaps a design doesn't cover (sign-in, data source, compliance) and confirm the read-back. Two are marked NEEDS_CONFIRMATION.

intake.pitch: TaskBoard — a small team task board. Build it to match the design in documentation/design/ (mockup.html + tokens.css + design-notes.md): a Board screen with To do / In progress / Done columns of task cards, a Task detail screen, and a Settings screen.
intake.roles: One role: team member. Everyone can create, edit, move and delete tasks, and set their own display name. No admin tier.
intake.signIn: Simple email + password, no SSO for launch. NEEDS_CONFIRMATION.
intake.dataSource: No backend yet — build against a stand-in (mock) data layer for tasks. Data shape from the design: task = { id, title, assignee, status (To do | In progress | Done), dueDate }.
intake.styling: Use the design's tokens verbatim (documentation/design/tokens.css): primary #2563eb, Inter. Do not invent a new palette.

designReadback._comment: Confirm the read-back the workflow presents at Intake. These are the design-derived facts it should surface; approve them.
designReadback.confirm: Yes — the screens, fields, colours and copy read back match the design. Proceed.
designReadback.uncertaintyToConfirm: Due-date format was not specified in the design. Use ISO (2026-05-01) for now. NEEDS_CONFIRMATION.

designUpdate._comment: PHASE 2 (#15): after the first build merges, drop the files from ../design-taskboard/update/docs/ into documentation/design/ (replacing the originals), then start ONE ordinary piece of work with the instruction below. Only the named screens should change; the Settings screen must be left alone; the earlier decisions (e.g. sign-in email+password) must survive the re-read.
designUpdate.instruction: Rebuild the Board and Task detail screens to match my updated design. Leave Settings as it is.
expectedChanges: Board: the 'New task' button is renamed to 'Add task'
Board: the assignee filter moves from top-left to top-right
Task detail: add a 'Priority' field (Low | Medium | High)

conflict._comment: The updated design contradicts an earlier decision, so the workflow must ASK which wins rather than silently overwrite.
conflict.designNowSays: tokens.css in the update sets --color-primary to #7c3aed (purple).
conflict.answer: Keep the blue #2563eb — the earlier decision wins over the design file. NEEDS_CONFIRMATION.
